text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait to impose 48-dinar ($158) annual health insurance fee on all expatriates. About 1.2 million foreigners live in Kuwait, which provides free health services to its 720,000 nationals.
- Niger's President Mainassara leaves Kuwait after three-day visit.
- Acting Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah returns after private visits to Britain, Italy.
- Firm activity at Kuwait Stock Exchange hits real estate market.
- Interior minister pushes for law to collect weapons held by people in Kuwait. Many kept weapons left by Iraq's troops after 1991 liberation from seven-month occupation.
- Livestock Trade & Transport Company KATT.KW says 1996 net profit amounted to 3.9 million dinars.
- United Nations expected to maintain sanctions on Iraq.
- Armed men rob petrol station. State-owned Kuwait National Petroleum Company, which runs some 80 stations, has said it plans to enhance security after several reported armed attacks.
